# ADR-053a — Amendment to ADR-053: every Google authorization MUST send `include_granted_scopes=true` — consent is per app, not per client

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Amendment to ADR-053 (2026-09-01, Checkpoint 7.8A): EVERY Google authorization this project builds MUST send `include_granted_scopes=true` — Gmail and Google Health alike. Consent in Google's linked-app model is per APP, not per client, so a non-additive consent REVOKES the other integrations.** Although this amends ADR-053 (a mail decision), it binds Health too, because the defect is a property of the shared consent screen rather than of either integration: ADR-046's three-scope Health grant is destroyed by a non-additive Gmail consent and vice versa, so a fix applied to one alone is not a fix at all. ADR-053's client-separation reasoning is corrected here, not rewritten: its conclusion that "a token minted for one integration is never reused for another" remains true and remains the rule. What was wrong was an unstated assumption resting on it — that separate OAuth clients within one Google Cloud project therefore yield separate *grants*. They do not. **Why `false` was chosen originally.** Least privilege, and the instinct was right: `packages/mail-providers/src/gmail-oauth.ts` set it under the comment "Never silently widen a grant by inheriting scopes from another client", so a Gmail token could not quietly acquire Calendar or Health authority. The same file already guarded the adjacent hazard, documenting that `prompt=consent` on every reconnect "would slowly destroy older grants — including, in this project, the Calendar and Health ones, which share the same Google account." The shared-account risk was understood; it was closed on one door and left open on another. **Why the assumption is disproved — by production evidence, not by argument.** Checkpoint 7.2's Gmail consent at `2026-08-31T23:04Z` replaced the entire "Personal OS" grant. The owner's Google Account linked-app panel afterwards reads *Access given on 2026-08-31* with **`gmail.metadata` as the only permission**, and Personal OS is **absent** from the account's Calendar-access list — a falsification test, not a confirmation. Each dependent failure is then simply the next token refresh after the grant set changed: Google Calendar `auth_expired` at 23:15Z (**+11 min**) and Google Health `invalid_grant` / `auth_permanent` with `request_count = 0` at 00:00:06Z (**+56 min**), the latter refused at the refresh grant before any API call. Two integrations that had run for months stopped within an hour of an unrelated integration's consent. **Why `true` is now required.** `include_granted_scopes=false` does not merely decline to widen the new TOKEN; it makes the consent NON-ADDITIVE, so the grant it produces *defines* the app's authority and everything previously granted is dropped. `true` selects Google's documented incremental authorization, under which the new consent is ADDED to what the account already granted. This is a correctness requirement, not a preference: without it, connecting any one integration destroys the others, and the defect is **reproducible in production** the moment Gmail consent is granted there. **Symmetry is load-bearing, which is why this amendment binds Health as well.** `packages/health-providers/src/google-health-oauth.ts` carried the identical `include_granted_scopes: "false"`, so with Gmail additive and Health not, reauthorizing Health would revoke Gmail and Calendar — the same incident, during the recovery meant to end it. Both are now `true`, on both the forced-consent and reconnect paths. **Google Calendar is a distinct case and is deliberately NOT changed here**: its Phase 4 flow is the native Play Services `AuthorizationRequest` (`apps/mobile/modules/google-calendar-auth`), which builds no OAuth URL and exposes no equivalent parameter, so the knob does not exist to set. Whether that flow is additive is **unverified**; the evidence only shows its grant can be destroyed BY another consent, not that its own consent destroys others. Until it is proven or changed — a native-module change, hence a new APK and a `versionCode` bump — the operational rule is that **Calendar is reconnected FIRST and the two additive consents follow**, so anything its consent might drop is re-added. **Why this does not violate least privilege.** The scopes Personal OS REQUESTS are unchanged. Mail remains exactly `gmail.metadata` — no `gmail.readonly`, no body, no send, reply, delete, archive, mark-read, move or label, and ADR-052's prohibition on acting on mail is untouched. Health remains exactly ADR-046's three `.readonly` scopes, and still never the fourth (`googlehealth.settings.readonly`) that ADR-046 cut along with paired-device support. Tests now name the forbidden scopes individually on both sides, so a future edit that adds one fails in the suite rather than at a consent screen. What changes is only that the account's other, separately-consented grants survive the transaction. The honest cost, stated rather than discovered: the access token Google returns may now carry previously granted scopes as well, so **Checkpoint 7.2's assertion that Google echoed *exactly* `gmail.metadata` no longer holds** and any test pinning it must be corrected rather than loosened. That is accepted because breadth of scope on a token is not capability exercised — the Gmail client is read-only by construction, exposes no mutation method at all, and calls only Gmail endpoints — and because the alternative is destroying two working integrations, which is a strictly larger loss of the user's own access. **Why a separate Google Cloud project remains rejected.** A second project would give a genuinely independent consent screen and independent grants, and would also fix this. It is **forbidden by ADR-051**, which states that no second development OAuth application, client, project, account or credential set exists or may be used. That decision is Locked and is not reopened here. **Everything else in ADR-053 is unchanged**: `gmail.metadata` only, `gmail.readonly` deliberately not requested, identity and the bootstrap cursor from a single `users.getProfile` call, the opaque `historyId` cursor with 404 → `needs_full_resync` as a first-class transition, `Retry-After` honoured, the closed `MailSyncErrorCode` enum, global digests, and quiet hours delaying rather than suppressing. Token storage, AES-256-GCM encryption, the hash-only single-use OAuth state and its redirect binding are all untouched (Checkpoint 7.8A, 2026-09-01)
